basics.name: Interactive mechanism demo sites: Wolfram Demonstrations Project (Machines / Mechanical Engineering topics), Colorado State University 'Engineering and Physics Video Demonstrations' (Mechanisms section), and MechSimulator (Mechanisms & Machines simulators)
basics.url: Wolfram: https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/topic/machines (JavaScript app; its data comes from https://www.wolframcloud.com/obj/resourcesystem/published/DemonstrationRepository/json/topic/machines.json); CSU: https://video-demos.colostate.edu/mechanics/mechanisms/ (plus /cams/ and /linkages/ sub-pages); MechSimulator: https://mechsimulator.com/mechanisms/
basics.resource_type: interactive tool / video channel (three separate sites: a large peer-reviewed library of interactive Wolfram Language 'Manipulate' models; a university lecturer's index page of short demo videos, photos and GIFs; and a single-author set of browser-based mechanism simulators)
basics.cost: Free for all three. Wolfram: free to view and use in the browser; editing or authoring needs Mathematica/Wolfram Language (paid) or a free Wolfram Cloud account. CSU: free. MechSimulator: free, no signup, funded by Google AdSense ads
basics.license: Wolfram: all content is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 Unported (terms page); you may link freely and reuse with attribution for non-commercial work, and derivatives must be shared alike. CSU: no licence stated; footer is '(c) 2026 Colorado State University', so treat as all rights reserved and link only [uncertain]. MechSimulator: all rights reserved; the Terms of Use allow sharing direct links but forbid copying, mirroring, scraping or reproducing its code or content without written permission
basics.year: Wolfram: launched May 2007 with Mathematica 6 (almost 1,300 Demonstrations at launch); site index last modified 29 Aug 2026; e.g. the Geneva Drive demo was published 19 Dec 2008 and last modified 21 Aug 2024. CSU: long-running site by Dr David Alciatore; start year not stated on the pages opened, current WordPress site with (c) 2026 footer [uncertain]. MechSimulator: start year not stated [uncertain]; Mechanisms page 'Updated 23 September 2026', Terms last updated 7 April 2026
basics.access_barrier: Wolfram: none to view in the browser (JavaScript + Wolfram Cloud; Cloudflare-protected), optional free Wolfram Player desktop app or Mathematica to run the downloadable notebooks offline. CSU: none (direct MP4 links and YouTube). MechSimulator: none (runs client-side in the browser, no account)
basics.image_license: Wolfram: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, but the preview animations, pop-up snapshots and 'link to this Demonstration' images are ALSO licensed under the MIT License (reusable anywhere, even commercially, if the copyright notice is kept), which makes Wolfram snapshot images the most reusable visuals of the three. CSU: videos, photos and GIFs have no stated licence, some are third-party (YouTube, HowStuffWorks, Woodward Governor animations) [uncertain]. MechSimulator: all rights reserved (owner Naseel Ibnu Azeez)
basics.authority_level: Wolfram: community-contributed but editorially reviewed before publication, each demo carries named authors and a permanent citation (strong 'educator/community, reviewed'). CSU: educator (Dr David Alciatore, Colorado State University mechanical engineering). MechSimulator: educator (single mechanical engineering instructor, M.Tech Machine Design; formulas from Shigley, Norton, Hibbeler), not peer-reviewed

coverage.covers: Wolfram: 13,216 Demonstrations overall; the Machines topic lists 325 and Mechanical Engineering 290 (483 unique across both). Mechanism content includes linkages (four-bar, coupler-curve atlas, Theo Jansen, Klann, Chebyshev walking, Peaucellier/Hart inversors, Sarrus, Bricard 6R, pantograph, quick-return, slider-crank, Scotch yoke), cams (radial cam design, cylindrical cam, idealized cam-follower), gears (involute, cycloidal, elliptic, hyperboloidal, planetary gear train, noncircular planetary, continuously variable planetary transmission, gearless cycloidal speed reducer, 5-speed manual transmission), intermittent motion (Geneva drive, Graham escapement), couplings and clutches (Oldham coupling, universal joint, positive-contact claw clutch, gyroscopic joint), and small clever devices (quick-release linkage, fastening mechanism using a rocker, spring return button, wave spring, cylinder-lock key cutting). CSU: about 70 links on the General mechanisms page plus 16 on Cams and 11 on Linkages: real-hardware videos (bowling pinsetter mechanisms, automobile differential, planetary gear drive, worm drive, lead-screw overhaul, ratcheted CVT, spherical scissor linkage, Thompson coupling vs CV joint vs U-joint, washing-machine museum) and cam/linkage photos. MechSimulator: 17 tools on the Mechanisms & Machines page in 4 topics (linkages/cams/intermittent motion 5, power transmission 3, dynamics 5, bearings & machine elements 4), including four-bar linkage, slider-crank, Scotch yoke/double-slider (Oldham coupling, elliptical trammel), cam & follower, Geneva mechanism (3-8 slots), gear trains (simple, compound, worm), manual synchromesh gearbox, belt & chain drive, power screw (self-locking); the whole site has 89 simulators per its About page (the sitemap lists 144 tool URLs)
coverage.organisation: Wolfram: topic tree (Engineering & Technology > Machines, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics ...) plus A-Z index, search, 'related Demonstrations' and 'more by author'; each topic page is a flat list of thumbnails. Works for browsing pictures, but finding things needs the proper term, and mechanism demos are mixed with maths curiosities (e.g. hinged dissections, clocks). CSU: one hand-written alphabetical-ish bullet list per page (General / Cams / Linkages), organised by example machine rather than mechanism type; easy to skim but not searchable by function. MechSimulator: by course topic in textbook order (kinematics > transmission > dynamics > machine elements), with a helpful 'What each mechanism converts' table (input motion > output motion > typical use); the best of the three for a beginner who thinks in terms of motion
coverage.scope_match: medium: together they animate many in-scope mechanism TYPES (Geneva drive, cams, Scotch yoke, planetary/worm/cycloidal gear trains, Oldham and universal couplings, claw clutch, quick-release linkage, ratcheted CVT, self-locking power screw), but they are teaching demos for motion and kinematics, not a catalogue of connections; almost nothing on snap fits, print-in-place, compliant joints, powered latches or adhesives
coverage.taxonomy_used: Wolfram: subject topic tree with 14 top-level topics (Mathematics, Computation, Physical Sciences, Life Sciences, Business & Social Systems, Systems Models & Methods, Engineering & Technology, Our World, Creative Arts, Kids & Fun, Programming Functionality ...), with Engineering & Technology split into 12 subtopics including Machines, Mechanical Engineering and Robotics; no mechanism taxonomy. CSU: by engineering course area (Controls, Mechanics > Dynamics / Mechanisms (General, Cams, Linkages) / Solid Mechanics / Vibration, Energy, Mathematics ...). MechSimulator: 9 site categories; Mechanisms page uses 4 groups following a 'theory of machines' course (Linkages, Cams & Intermittent Motion / Power Transmission / Dynamics of Machines / Bearings & Machine Elements) plus a motion-conversion table
coverage.example_types: Geneva drive (Maltese cross) [Wolfram, MechSimulator]; Scotch yoke [Wolfram, MechSimulator, CSU]; Oldham coupling [Wolfram, MechSimulator]; universal joint (Hooke's joint) [Wolfram]; Thompson constant-velocity coupling [CSU]; positive-contact claw clutch (dog clutch) [Wolfram]; quick-release linkage [Wolfram]; fastening mechanism using a rocker [Wolfram]; spring return button [Wolfram]; wave spring / wave spring washer [Wolfram]; planetary (epicyclic) gear train [Wolfram, CSU]; gearless cycloidal speed reducer [Wolfram]; continuously variable planetary transmission [Wolfram]; ratcheted continuously variable transmission [CSU]; worm drive [CSU, MechSimulator]; automobile differential [CSU]; desmodromic (closed-form) cams [CSU]; cylindrical (barrel) cam [Wolfram]; Graham clock escapement [Wolfram]; Peaucellier straight-line linkage [Wolfram, CSU]; Sarrus linkage [Wolfram]; spherical (geodesic) scissor linkage [CSU]; self-locking power screw [MechSimulator]; swash plate drive [Wolfram]
coverage.making_methods: General engineering / theory of machines teaching; nothing aimed at 3D printing, CNC or hobby robotics (CSU also has robotics and mechatronics sections)
coverage.item_count: Wolfram: 13,216 Demonstrations in total; 483 in the Machines and Mechanical Engineering topics, of which roughly 100 are about linkages, cams, gears, couplings and similar mechanisms. CSU: about 100 mechanism links (about 70 general, 16 cams, 11 linkages). MechSimulator: 17 mechanism tools (89 simulators site-wide per the About page)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Indexing/intermittent motion: yes (Geneva drive in Wolfram and MechSimulator, with dwell and locking phases shown; Graham escapement). Gear trains/gearboxes: yes (planetary, compound, worm, cycloidal reducer, CVTs, differential, manual synchromesh gearbox). Self-locking: yes in MechSimulator's power-screw tool (self-locking condition) and CSU's lead-screw 'overhaul' (back-driving) video. One-way/ratchet: only CSU's ratcheted CVT video [uncertain]. Over-centre / hand-release: only indirectly (Wolfram 'Quick Release Linkage' and 'Fastening Mechanism Using a Rocker') [uncertain]. Torque-limiting: not found. Compliant: only wave springs and a bistable octahedron (Wolfram), no compliant-joint demos. Print-in-place: none. Powered connectors: none as latches (CSU's Actuators page only shows motors, a voice coil, pneumatic cylinders and a shape-memory-alloy walking robot). Adhesives: none
coverage.entry_structure: Wolfram: title, author(s), live interactive model with sliders ('Manipulate'), snapshots, short caption/details, categories, related demos, permanent citation, downloadable source notebook, embed code. CSU: one-line link text to an MP4, GIF, photo or YouTube video; no written explanation. MechSimulator: animated canvas with sliders, live graphs, presets, four modes (Simulate, Explore, Practice, Quiz), SI/imperial units, and a written user guide explaining the mechanism and its phases
coverage.audience_level: Wolfram: high school to research (mostly undergraduate). CSU: undergraduate engineering. MechSimulator: diploma, apprenticeship and polytechnic students (early undergraduate)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: moving pictures make mechanisms easy to grasp and MechSimulator explains each one in plain language with a motion-conversion table, but Wolfram captions are terse and assume maths vocabulary, and CSU gives only link titles with no explanation
usefulness.has_images: yes: Wolfram snapshots are clean computer renderings (MIT-licensed); CSU has real photos of engines, cam followers, bike linkages (variable quality, some old); MechSimulator draws clear 2D diagrams on canvas
usefulness.has_animations: yes, the main strength: Wolfram interactive 3D/2D models with sliders running in the browser via Wolfram Cloud; CSU real-hardware MP4 videos, GIF animations and high-speed video; MechSimulator animated, adjustable browser simulations with live velocity/acceleration graphs
usefulness.gaps: No connection-level content (snap fits, clips, latches, detents, print-in-place, compliant hinges, adhesives, powered latches); no design rules for 3D printing; no CAD or STL downloads; no function-based finder; Wolfram needs the right keyword and mixes in unrelated maths; CSU is a link list without explanations and some links point to third-party or dead sites [uncertain]; MechSimulator covers only about a dozen classic mechanisms
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes for Wolfram (stable per-demo URLs, e.g. https://resources.wolframcloud.com/DemonstrationRepository/web/GenevaDriveMalteseCross/ or https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/GenevaDriveMalteseCross/) and MechSimulator (per-tool URLs, e.g. https://mechsimulator.com/tools/geneva-mechanism/); CSU is best linked at page level, or to individual MP4 files on video-demos.colostate.edu, which are less stable [uncertain]
usefulness.reusable_data: Wolfram: structured and exportable: public JSON files (all.json index of every demo, topics-tree.json, per-topic and per-demo JSON with authors, dates, categories, snapshots and notebook links) used by the site itself; the list and content are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), snapshot images MIT. CSU: scrape-only, no licence. MechSimulator: not reusable (terms forbid scraping and mirroring); link only
usefulness.maintained: Wolfram: yes, active (index last modified 29 Aug 2026; new demos still published). CSU: online and still edited (2026 footer) but many outbound links are to old third-party pages (HowStuffWorks, rexresearch, skyshorz) that may be dead [uncertain]. MechSimulator: yes, very active (pages updated September 2026). Wayback Machine could not be checked from this environment
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) MechSimulator's 'What each mechanism converts' table (input motion > output motion > typical use) is a ready-made flow-chart layer for motion converters. (2) MechSimulator's presets (e.g. '6-slot indexing', 'film projector') show a type in real uses. (3) Wolfram's per-entry 'related' and 'more by author' links and permanent citations. (4) Embedding or linking a Wolfram live model or MIT-licensed snapshot next to an entry gives a free interactive picture. (5) CSU's approach of pairing a mechanism with a real everyday machine (bowling pinsetter, washing machine, car differential) helps beginners recognise where they have seen it. (6) Phase labels on animations (dwell, engage, drive, exit, lock) explain how a mechanism works step by step
usefulness.design_rules_given: Some, only in MechSimulator: Geneva geometry (R = a/tan(pi/n), dwell %, index angle), Grashof condition for four-bars, belt tension ratio, power-screw raising/lowering torque and self-locking condition, gear ratio/torque, bearing life (ISO 281), AGMA gear strength; Wolfram demos compute geometry but rarely state rules; CSU none. Nothing on printed clearances
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Yes, in a limited way: every Wolfram demo is a parametric model whose source notebook can be downloaded and edited in the Wolfram Language (not CAD); MechSimulator lets you change dimensions and read off values but gives no geometry export
usefulness.file_formats: Wolfram: web interactive, PNG snapshots, .nb notebook source (CDF/Wolfram Player). CSU: MP4 video, GIF, JPG/PNG, one PPS PowerPoint, YouTube links. MechSimulator: HTML/JavaScript canvas only (values can be copied)
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: Wolfram titles and CSU captions use proper engineering names (Oldham coupling, Graham escapement, Peaucellier inversor, desmodromic cam), and MechSimulator explains terms like inversion, dwell and self-locking in plain words; none gives aliases or translations
usefulness.decision_support: Only MechSimulator's motion-conversion comparison table and a bearing-selection tool (choose among eight bearing types by life, load and lubrication); no selector or flow chart in Wolfram or CSU
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Independent originals. Wolfram demos by many authors (e.g. Sandor Kabai wrote Geneva Drive, Oldham Coupling and Claw Clutch); MechSimulator draws on Shigley, Norton, Hibbeler and Cengel textbooks; CSU mixes Alciatore's own videos with links to HowStuffWorks, YouTube, Cornell KMODDL and animatedengines.com. Overlaps with DMG-Lib, KMODDL, Mecapedia animations and Nguyen Duc Thang's mechanism animations for classic linkages, cams and Geneva drives. Note that search results also show a differently named browser simulator ('MechSim'), which is not the same site as MechSimulator [uncertain]
